content.text: I have inspected every "exclusive"/exclusivity hit, the Manufacturing & Supply article, the Commercialization/co-promotion mechanic, the covenants article and the competing-product termination trigger. No exclusivity binds Sanofi.

input.quote: (i) Sanofi may subcontract to Third Parties the performance of Sanofi's tasks and obligations with respect to the Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of any Product as Sanofi deems appropriate
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Sanofi, so it meets the preferred position. Every "exclusive" provision either runs in our favour or is not a sourcing restraint: Section 3.1(a) grants Sanofi an exclusive licence (even as to RevMed), Section 3.5(a) is a non-compete binding RevMed, and Section 13.2(q) confirms no third-party exclusivity limits our rights. Section 3.4(c) expressly lets Sanofi subcontract Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization to Third Parties as it deems appropriate, and Article VII contains no requirements/sole-source commitment (Section 7.3 only contemplates a negotiated Supply Agreement where one Party in fact manufactures for the other, and Section 7.2 obliges RevMed to help Sanofi stand up its own third-party supply). RevMed's Section 8.7 Co-Promotion Option is a one-time right to a capped share of US Detailing, not a prohibition on our use of alternatives, and Section 12.2(d) is a conditional termination trigger for a Competing Product rather than an exclusive-dealing covenant (and belongs to the termination rule in any event). No redline proposed; nothing here restricts our freedom to source from others.
